findings.issue: “Constant means pure” overstates the conclusion. Constant elemental mass ratios support purity but do not prove it: a mixture can have the same composition across multiple samples. Replace with “constant supports purity; changing indicates a mixture.”
findings.evidence: The source's answer_move says, “A constant ratio supports a pure substance,” rather than establishing purity conclusively.

findings.issue: “Not tested: n, l, mₗ, mₛ” broadens the exclusion from assigning quantum numbers to excluding the quantities altogether. State that assigning quantum numbers to individual electrons is not assessed; shell numbers and subshell structure remain relevant.
findings.evidence: The CED exclusion specifically states: “The assignment of quantum numbers to electrons in subshells of an atom will not be assessed on the AP Exam.”

findings.issue: The NEW trend statement should say first ionization energy “generally increases” across a period. Its unqualified wording can mislead students on AP-relevant exceptions caused by subshell energies and electron pairing, such as Be/B and N/O.
findings.evidence: First ionization energy decreases from Be to B and from N to O despite increasing nuclear charge. The broad trend is AP-appropriate, but it is not monotonic.

findings.issue: “Not tested: Cr and Cu exceptions” is too broad. Specify that writing configurations that are exceptions to the Aufbau principle is excluded; this is not a blanket exclusion of chromium, copper, or their properties.
findings.evidence: The CED exclusion is specifically: “Writing the electron configuration of elements that are exceptions to the aufbau principle will not be assessed on the AP Exam.”

findings.issue: The Do line drops the restriction to common main-group ions. Counting valence electrons from the group and gaining or losing electrons to reach a noble-gas configuration is not a general method for predicting transition-metal ion charges. Restore “For common main-group ions.”
findings.evidence: The source's answer_move explicitly begins “For common main-group ions.” Common ions such as Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺ do not have noble-gas configurations.
